questions.question:
**Directions: In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

To bring these to you (1)/wherever you are (2)/however you have time (3) / No error (4)/
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'however you have time'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In this given part of the sentence, the usage of **'however'** is incorrect Instead, use** 'whenever'**

 
• According to the rule of grammar, we need to use 'conjunction' that denotes time hence the conjunction 'whenever' shows the time So it is the correct conjunction. Also, it means 'You use whenever to refer to any time or every time that something happens or is true.'
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She always called at the house whenever she was in the area.
 
 

**Correct sentence - **To bring these to you wherever you are** whenever** you have time.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

We will continue to (1)/strive in dark (2)/but we will not driven out (3) / No error (4)/
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of future verb is brought under consideration. Helping verb 'will/shall' takes verb's first form i.e V1. Hence, replace 'driven' with **drive. **Thus, **option 3 **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **We will continue to strive in dark but we will not drive out.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She cannot deprive him______his rights.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. Verb 'deprive' means suffering a severe and damaging lack of basic material and cultural benefits; underprivileged. So, when the subject is deprived of something(noun). Then, preposition 'of' is used. If it is a verb(deprived from going). Then, 'from' is used. Hence, **option 3 i.e. of **is correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

My uncle, Mr. Lalit Singh comes home at the _______ of the month.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Since the blank has article before it, it cannot be filled with a verb. Thus, the noun **end **is appropriate answer.

Hence, **option 1 **is correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best express the meaning of the given word.**

Awe
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Admiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Awe"** means a feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder. (विस्मय)

 
 
• **Example: **The tourists were in awe of the magnificent waterfall.
 
 
 
• **"Admiration" **refers to respect and warm approval. (प्रशंसा)
 
 
• **Example: **She looked at her mentor with admiration.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word that best expresses the meaning of "Awe" is "Admiration".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Admiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Expectation **(अपेक्षा): A strong belief that something will happen or be the case.

 
 
• **Example:** There is a high expectation for the new policy to bring positive change.
 
 
 
• **Familiarity **(परिचय): Close acquaintance with or knowledge of something.
 
 
• **Example: **Her familiarity with the local culture helped her settle in quickly.
 
 
 
• **Calmness** (शांति): The state or quality of being free from agitation or strong emotion.
 
 
• **Example:** He maintained his calmness even under pressure.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best express the meaning of the given word.**

Rejuvenate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Update**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Rejuvenate"** means to make someone or something look or feel younger, fresher, or more lively. (पुनः युवा करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The spa treatment rejuvenated her and made her feel years younger.
 
 
 
• **"Update"** refers to making something more modern or up to date. (अद्यतन)
 
 
• **Example:** We need to update our software to the latest version.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the best word to express the meaning of 'Rejuvenate' is 'Update'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Update**.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Destroy** (विनाश करना): To cause something to end or no longer exist.

 
 
• **Example:** The fire destroyed the entire building.
 
 
 
• **Rain** (वर्षा): Water falling in drops from the sky.
 
 
• **Example:** The rain started pouring down heavily in the afternoon.
 
 
 
• **Exhaust** (थकाना): To tire someone out completely.
 
 
• **Example:** The marathon run exhausted him.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Augment
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Degrade.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The opposite in meaning of the word **"augment"** is** "degrade,"** so the correct answer is** option 3.**
 
• The word** "augment" **means **to increase or make something larger in size or quantity**.
 
 
• For example, "She **augmented **her income by taking on a second job" means that she increased her income by taking on a second job.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 3, "degrade," which means to lower in quality, value, or status.
 
 
• For example, "The quality of the product **degraded** over time" means that the quality of the product declined over time.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1, "develop,"** means to grow or progress, and it is not an antonym of **"augment."**

 
 
• For example, "The company is **developing **a new product" means that the company is creating a new product.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "enhance,"** means to improve or make something better. It is not an antonym of "augment," but the two words are related.
 
 
• For example, "The new technology **enhanced **the user experience" means that the new technology improved the user experience.
 
 
 
• **Option 4, "increase," **means to make something larger or more numerous. This word is similar in meaning to "augment" but it is not an antonym.
 
 
• For example, "The company **increased **its profits by 20%" means that the company's profits grew by 20%.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

(Being a cold day), we cancelled our picnic.

options.text: It having been a cold day

questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1 **

When one action occurs in the course of another. And, the time gap between them is very little. So, following pattern is used :-

Subject + being + object, rest of the sentence.

Hence, add **it **at the starting. So, **option 1 **is the appropriate answer.

questions.solution:

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

The opinion

P: opinion of many

Q: great must be the

R: that makes a book
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Firstly, the starter ends with 'opinion'. Hence, it cannot continue with the same word. So, option 3 is eliminated. Also, an article is followed by either a noun or an adjective. Hence, sequence QR in option 4 is incorrect. Since, starter ends with a noun and Q starts with an adjective. But, this is grammatically incorrect because adjective comes before noun. Hence, option 2 is incorrect. Hence, **option 1 i.e. RQP **is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Hint :- Conjunction 'as long as'.

sneak - move or go in a furtive or stealing way.

questions.question: In the winter______,

Clearly, winter season is described in the complete passage. Thus, **option 2 i.e. season **is suitable for the blank. 

Note :- We cannot use 'climate' because it means the weather conditions prevailing in an area in general or over a long period.

But seasons are regular in a year and observed in all the areas.

questions.question: Clear however sometimes it remains _______all through
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Thick layer of fog is present in the atmosphere during winter season. Since, fog is not transparent in nature and it makes the view unclear. Hence, **option 3 i.e. unclear **is the suitable answer.

questions.question: season and makes condition_______,
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

We know there is a different rainy season in part of a year. But, when it rains during winter season, it clearly makes the condition worse(bad or poor).

Note :- Since, the whole passage describes the poor condition faced during winter season. Hence, options 2 & 4 are clearly eliminated. Also, 'abnormal' means not normal, unusual, rare. And, we cannot use rare for a seasonal condition. Hence, **option 1 i.e. worse **is the appropriate answer.
